references.name: Blaise Pascal
references.desc: Co-founder of probability theory; Pascal's Triangle and the famous wager on God's existence

references.name: Pierre de Fermat
references.desc: Correspondence with Pascal that birthed probability theory; brilliant amateur mathematician

references.name: Jacob Bernoulli
references.desc: Ars Conjectandi — discovered the Law of Large Numbers; proved that enough observations reveal true probability

references.name: Daniel Bernoulli
references.desc: St. Petersburg Paradox paper; introduced utility theory — value depends on circumstances, not just amount

references.name: Abraham de Moivre
references.desc: Normal distribution and standard deviation; Doctrine of Chances

references.name: Thomas Bayes
references.desc: Bayesian inference — updating prior beliefs with new evidence; published posthumously by Richard Price

references.name: Carl Friedrich Gauss
references.desc: Bell curve / Gaussian distribution; Theoria Motus on estimating planetary orbits

references.name: Francis Galton
references.desc: Regression to the mean; the Quincunx device; eugenics movement; Hereditary Genius

references.name: John Graunt
references.desc: Pioneer of demographics; first to generalize from mortality records to population statistics (1660s)

references.name: Edmund Halley
references.desc: First proper life table using Breslau mortality data; foundation of actuarial science

references.name: John Maynard Keynes
references.desc: Radical uncertainty vs. calculable risk; criticized overreliance on classical probability

references.name: Frank Knight
references.desc: Risk, Uncertainty, and Profit — distinguished measurable risk from true uncertainty

references.name: Kenneth Arrow
references.desc: Nobel laureate; proved impossibility of perfect decision-making under uncertainty

references.name: Harry Markowitz
references.desc: Modern Portfolio Theory — diversification as the only free lunch in finance

references.name: Daniel Kahneman & Amos Tversky
references.desc: Prospect Theory — loss aversion, mental accounting, and systematic cognitive biases

references.name: Louis Bachelier
references.desc: The Theory of Speculation (1900) — first mathematical model of market randomness

references.name: Fischer Black & Myron Scholes
references.desc: Black-Scholes option pricing model; transformed derivatives markets

references.name: Richard Thaler
references.desc: Behavioral economics; showed investors overreact to recent news and lose sight of the long run

references.name: Girolamo Cardano
references.desc: Renaissance polymath; first serious analysis of probability in games of chance

references.name: Luca Paccioli
references.desc: Summa de arithmetica (1494) — posed the problem of dividing stakes that inspired Pascal and Fermat

references.name: Omar Khayyam
references.desc: Mathematician and poet; developed algebra using Hindu-Arabic numerals; reformed the calendar

references.name: Jeremy Bentham
references.desc: Rediscovered utility theory; utilitarian philosophy of maximizing happiness
